title: Divide by 1 to 10
subtitle: Times tables to 10, backwards
bounds: PROTOCOL 4c, facts range cartridge. Forms: R is p ÷ a = ? (answer the quotient), C is p ÷ ? = b (answer the divisor), S is ? ÷ a = b (answer the dividend); p = a × b, the times table read backwards, never ÷ 0, no 0 ÷ ? = 0. Divisors and quotients 0-10. T1 R: a or b in {0,1,2,5,10}. T2 R: facts of 3, 4, 9 (a, b both in {3,4,9} at least 8). T3 R: facts of 6, 7, 8 (a, b both in {6,7,8} at least 8). T4 C: a, b in {3,4,6,7,8,9} (at least 12) plus C with a, b 2-10. T5 S: a, b in {3,4,6,7,8,9} (at least 12) plus C on the same pairs. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers up to 999, at least 2 near and at most 1 far. R: near within 2 of the quotient (GROUP_OFF q+-1, +-2), far SUBTRACTED p-a, MULTIPLIED p×a, TENS_SLIP q+-10. C: near within 2 of the divisor (MISSING_ONE_OFF a+-1, ARITH +-2), far MISSING_SUBTRACTED p-b, MISSING_MULTIPLIED p×b. S: near within the larger factor of the dividend (START_GROUP_OFF p+-a, START_ADDED a+b, START_TENS p+-10 when a factor is 11 or more, with a twin ones digit when p is 20 or more). The answer's rank among the four values is spread 15-35% per tier.

tiers.name: Easy: 0, 1, 2, 5, 10
tiers.description: Divide by 1, 2, 5 and 10, and 0 divided by a number.

tiers.name: Facts with 3, 4, 9
tiers.description: Divide by 3, 4 and 9 using the fact family.

tiers.name: Facts with 6, 7, 8
tiers.description: Divide by 6, 7 and 8. Think: what times it makes this?

tiers.name: Missing divisors
tiers.description: Find the divisor: 42 ÷ ? = 7. Think 7 times what.

GROUP_OFF.student: Close: a group or two off. Multiply your answer by the divisor to check.
GROUP_OFF.teacher: Quotient off by one or two: counted a group or two too many or too few.

SUBTRACTED.student: Divide, don't subtract. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend (p − a) instead of dividing.

MULTIPLIED.student: Divide, don't multiply. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies dividend and divisor (p × a) instead of dividing.

TENS_SLIP.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply back to check the size.
TENS_SLIP.teacher: Quotient off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.

MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: One off. Try your number in the problem: does the division work out?
MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing divisor off by one: stopped a fact early or late in the table.

MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Don't subtract. Ask: what times the answer shown makes the dividend?
MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts (p − b) to find the missing divisor instead of asking what times b makes p.

MISSING_MULTIPLIED.student: Too big. Divide the dividend by your number: is it the answer shown?
MISSING_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies (p × b) to find the missing divisor instead of dividing or asking what times b makes p.

START_GROUP_OFF.student: One group off. Multiply the two numbers you see, no more, no less.
START_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Missing dividend off by one divisor (a × (b +- 1)): counted one group too many or too few.

START_ADDED.student: Don't add. To undo dividing, multiply the two numbers you see.
START_ADDED.teacher: Adds the divisor and quotient (a + b) to find the missing dividend instead of multiplying back.

START_TENS.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply the two numbers, then check the size.
START_TENS.teacher: Missing dividend off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.
